prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Houston after a car wreck. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first, a quick question so I recommend the best fit: do you have major/catastrophic injuries (hospitalized, long recovery, permanent impairment) or more minor injuries? Also, do you want a large national firm (more resources, heavy advertising) or a smaller Houston boutique (more personal attention)?

While you answer, here are immediate, practical steps and what to look for when calling firms — plus the types of Houston firms you should consider calling and why.

What to ask when you call (so you compare firms quickly)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases in Houston regularly? How many such cases did you handle last year?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (the named attorney, an associate, or a paralegal)?  
- Do you take cases on contingency? What is your fee percentage and any possible additional costs?  
- Do you have trial experience and past verdicts/settlements for car accidents? (Ask for recent examples.)  
- Will you advance medical and expert costs?  
- How do you communicate (phone/email/text) and how often will I receive updates?  
- Do you have experience with insurance companies and dealing with uninsured/underinsured motorist claims?  
- Can you provide references or recent client reviews?

Types of Houston firms to call — and why
- Large regional/national plaintiff firms (e.g., Morgan & Morgan, The Lanier Law Firm): Why call them — they have big teams, resources to hire experts, and experience handling high-value or complex claims. Good if injuries are severe and you may need long-term care or high damages.  
- Established Houston plaintiffs boutiques (local trial firms): Why call them — deep local court and judge knowledge, more personalized service, and often aggressive trial experience. Good if you want an attorney who knows local jury pools and courts.  
- Plaintiff firms that emphasize trial results: Why call them — having a reputation for going to trial increases leverage in settlement talks with insurers. Good if insurers are denying responsibility.  
- Firms experienced with uninsured/underinsured motorist claims and catastrophic injuries: Why call them — they can pursue additional avenues of recovery (third parties, UM/UIM, product liability).

Specific places to call (how to pick from these)
I can give a tailored shortlist if you tell me whether you want national resources or a local boutique and how severe your injuries are. If you prefer, I’ll provide 5–7 named Houston firms to call next (I’ll include a quick note on why each might be a fit and what to ask them). Which do you prefer: national firms, local boutiques, or a mix?
